approaches.approach: Ordinary surgery followed by transverse isotopy
approaches.result_and_obstruction: For a nonsingular closed 1-form alpha defining F, every positively F-transverse closed curve has positive alpha period; all curves in a zero-period homology class are excluded. Product fibre foliations have many such knots, so arbitrary Kirby links cannot simply be isotoped transverse. This blocks that proof method, not all surgery descriptions.

For surgery on L in N, pi1 of the filled manifold surjects onto pi1(N)/normal(L); abelianization yields b1(M)>=b1(N)-rank(span[L]). Therefore any fixed-target theorem needs unbounded link-component count on Sigma_g x S1. But 2g+1 disjoint positively transverse sections can normally generate the product group, so this quotient obstruction can disappear entirely.

A link positively transverse to a fibration is a finite braid. On each peripheral torus the original integral fibre class evaluates zero on meridian and positively (degree d_i) on longitude. By the Dehn-filling pi1 quotient, the restricted original class extends over surgery slope p_i mu_i+q_i lambda_i iff every q_i d_i=0; hence only original meridional fillings preserve that class. General surgery is permitted to destroy it, so no universal-target contradiction follows.

approaches.approach: Contact approximation and transverse surgery transfer
approaches.result_and_obstruction: On T3, beta_epsilon=dt+epsilon(cos(2pi t)dx+sin(2pi t)dy) is contact with wedge coefficient -2pi epsilon^2. The x-circle at t=y=0 is beta_epsilon-positive for all epsilon>0, but has dt-period zero and cannot be isotoped transverse to ker(dt). C0-closeness alone therefore does not transfer contact-transverse links back to the foliation. A uniform strict tangent margin exceeding the form perturbation is sufficient, but not supplied.

approaches.approach: Recurrent triangulations and directed-cycle surgery construction
approaches.result_and_obstruction: For a finite directed graph, every edge lies on a directed cycle iff a strictly positive integral circulation exists. Sum one return cycle per edge for sufficiency; a reachable-set cut proves necessity. For a graph actually embedded with positively transverse edges in a smooth cooriented foliation, cycle decomposition, monotone local smoothing and general-position perturbation realize a disjoint positive transverse link carrying every edge. This supplies a candidate surgery link, but no framing or handle-cancellation theorem forces its surgery manifold to be fixed. Calegari's stronger positive-cohomology orientation implies fibering and cannot silently replace his recurrent local orientation.

exclusions: Literature search, duplicate gate, diagnostics, audit and packaging are not author approaches.
